references.text: God gives instructions about the materials to be collected for the sanctuary, including gold, which is later accounted for in Exod 38:24.
The Israelites brought voluntary gifts of gold for the sanctuary, which is the same gold that is counted here.
The sanctuary shekel is mentioned as the standard weight, the same unit of measure used to weigh the gold.
The wave offering (תְּנוּפָה) is mentioned here; the same term is used for the gold given as 'wave gold' or a heave offering.
A similar accounting of gold and other metals given as offerings for the sanctuary at its consecration.
David gathered large amounts of gold for the temple, showing continuity in the use of gold for God's sanctuary.
David speaks about the gold he has collected for the house of the Lord, reflecting the holy work to which the gold was put.
Both verses document the total weight of the gold dedicated to the service of the Lord, in the wilderness sanctuary and after the Midianite war respectively.
Thematic parallel: the people give enormous amounts of gold and silver voluntarily for the building of God's house (tabernacle vs. temple).
